memory_update.text: For the HBM/advanced-packaging/test node, the highest-priority US-listed candidates are TSM, MU, AMKR, ASX, AMAT, KLAC, TER, FORM, ONTO, CAMT, KLIC, ENTG, LRCX, COHU, and ACMR.

Separate direct capacity operators and suppliers from tool/material enablers: TSM, MU, AMKR, and ASX are closer to physical capacity; AMAT, KLAC, LRCX, TER, FORM, ONTO, CAMT, KLIC, ENTG, COHU, and ACMR require evidence that AI/HBM packaging demand is material rather than generic semiconductor cyclicality.

Important HBM and substrate suppliers such as SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Nan Ya PCB, and other ABF/interposer ecosystem names are not primary US-listed common stocks; ADR/OTC or non-US coverage may be needed in a later global universe layer.

Substrate and silicon interposer pure-play exposure is limited in the US-listed universe; many US-listed candidates are indirect tool, materials, inspection, or OSAT proxies rather than pure substrate suppliers.

Best falsification checks for this node: CoWoS/HBM lead times normalize, HBM yields improve faster than expected, substrate supply is not limiting, AI accelerator demand shifts to less package-intensive architectures, or customers dual-source packaging/test capacity faster than expected.

summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI accelerator bottleneck node covering HBM supply, CoWoS-like advanced packaging, OSAT capacity, advanced packaging equipment, inspection/metrology, probe/test, and specialty materials. The strongest direct exposures are TSM, MU, AMKR, ASX, AMAT, KLAC, TER, FORM, ONTO, CAMT, KLIC, ENTG, LRCX, COHU, and ACMR. Key distinction: TSM/MU/AMKR/ASX are closer to capacity and qualification bottlenecks; AMAT/KLAC/LRCX/KLIC/ONTO/CAMT/FORM/TER/COHU/ENTG/ACMR are second-order enablers whose evidence should be checked through advanced packaging order commentary, utilization, backlog, and AI/HBM customer qualification rather than AI narrative alone.
